questions.passage: So, yes, reading a poem or novel, watching a film, looking at a piece of artwork, or watching an awe-inspiring athletic performance increases psychological richness. It requires our own interpretation of the poet’s, novelist’s, filmmaker’s, or artist’s personal beliefs and expression, and recognition of beauty in athletes’ extraordinary actions. In this sense, it differs from firsthand experiences gained through personal adventures. Nonetheless, we can still have very real, immediate experiences through arts and sports under the right circumstances.
questions.prompt: How are aesthetic and firsthand experiences distinguished?
options: Aesthetic experiences can never feel real or immediate.
Aesthetic experiences involve interpretation, yet can still feel real and immediate under suitable circumstances.
Firsthand adventures require no personal involvement.
Every exposure to art automatically gives all viewers the same experience.
questions.promptZh: 审美体验与亲身体验怎样区分？

亲身冒险不需本人参与。
每次接触艺术都自动使人人体验相同。
analyses: A nonetheless 后明确 real, immediate。
B own interpretation 与 under the right circumstances 两部分都保留。
C firsthand personal adventures 指本人直接参与。
D own interpretation 和条件限定不支持人人自动相同。本书结论不能把每次看艺术都当成保证增益。

we can still have very real, immediate experiences through arts and sports under the right circumstances.
